title: describe
description:
describe is used to group related tests and benchmarks into a suite. Suites help organize your test files by creating logical blocks, making test output easier to read and enabling shared setup/teardown through lifecycle hooks.

When you use test in the top level of file, they are collected as part of the implicit suite for it. Using describe you can define a new suite in the current context, as a set of related tests or benchmarks and other nested suites.

You can also nest describe blocks if you have a hierarchy of tests:

children.name: Test Options
children.description: You can use test options to apply configuration to every test inside a suite, including nested suites. This is useful when you want to set timeouts, retries, or other options for a group of related tests.

children.name: shuffle
children.description: Run tests within the suite in random order. This option is inherited by nested suites.

children.name: describe.skip
children.description: Use describe.skip in a suite to avoid running a particular describe block.

children.name: describe.skipIf
children.description: In some cases, you might run suites multiple times with different environments, and some of the suites might be environment-specific. Instead of wrapping the suite with if, you can use describe.skipIf to skip the suite whenever the condition is truthy.

children.name: describe.only
children.description:
Use describe.only to only run certain suites

Sometimes it is very useful to run only tests in a certain file, ignoring all other tests from the whole test suite, which pollute the output.

In order to do that, run vitest with specific file containing the tests in question:

children.name: describe.concurrent
children.description:
describe.concurrent runs all inner suites and tests in parallel

Set concurrent to false to opt out of concurrency inherited from a parent suite or sequence.concurrent:

.skip, .only, and .todo works with concurrent suites. All the following combinations are valid:

When running concurrent tests, Snapshots and Assertions must use expect from the local Test Context to ensure the right test is detected.

examples.code:
describe.concurrent(/* ... */)
describe.skip.concurrent(/* ... */) // or describe.concurrent.skip(/* ... */)
describe.only.concurrent(/* ... */) // or describe.concurrent.only(/* ... */)
describe.todo.concurrent(/* ... */) // or describe.concurrent.todo(/* ... */)

children.name: describe.shuffle
children.description:
Vitest provides a way to run all tests in random order via CLI flag --sequence.shuffle or config option sequence.shuffle, but if you want to have only part of your test suite to run tests in random order, you can mark it with this flag.

.skip, .only, and .todo works with random suites.

children.name: describe.todo
children.description: Use describe.todo to stub suites to be implemented later. An entry will be shown in the report for the tests so you know how many tests you still need to implement.

examples.code:
// An entry will be shown in the report for this suite
describe.todo('unimplemented suite')

children.name: describe.each
children.description: Use describe.each if you have more than one test that depends on the same data.
notes: TIPWhile describe.each is provided for Jest compatibility, Vitest also has describe.for which simplifies argument types and aligns with test.for.
First row should be column names, separated by |;
One or more subsequent rows of data supplied as template literal expressions using ${value} syntax.

children.name: describe.for
children.description: The difference from describe.each is how array case is provided in the arguments. Other non array case (including template string usage) works exactly same.
